subject: Data handling Q&A — non-training guarantee and retention windows
messages:
From: Emily Reed <emily.reed@gamma-analytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@gamma-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on data residency / retention / training use

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Our InfoSec and Legal teams had a few follow-ups so I wanted to put them in writing:

1) Training: Do you use customer-provided content (prompts, uploads, responses) to train or improve Redwood's foundation models or any shared models? If so, is that aggregated/anonymized, and is there an opt-out?

2) Retention: For hosted API customers, how long do you retain request/response payloads, KV caches, and debug logs by default? Can we shorten or disable retention for our tenant?

3) Deletion: If Gamma requests deletion (e.g., data subject request or contractual requirement), what is the SLA for removal from active systems, backups, and any analytics stores?

4) Residency: Our data must remain in the US (primary + backups). Can you confirm hosting regions and where logs or telemetry may be processed?

5) Contract/reference: We need explicit language in the DPA stating “Redwood does not use customer content to train models.” Will you agree to that, and can you provide a draft DPA/DSP to review?

Appreciate a concise answer we can pass to legal. Happy to schedule a short call if easier.

Best,
Emily Reed
InfoSec Lead, Gamma Analytics

Attachment: sample_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet with numbered items)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Reed <emily.reed@gamma-analytics.com>
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@gamma-analytics.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on data residency / retention / training use

Emily — thanks for the clear list. I’ll keep this short and then loop in our security/legal folks for any contractual language. High-level answers below (followed by attachments and next steps).

1) Training: Redwood does NOT use customer content submitted to a customer’s private tenancy or Dedicated capacity to train or improve our shared/base models. For Hosted API, customer content is not used to retrain base models by default. We do, however, collect limited telemetry (see #2) to maintain service health. We are willing to include an explicit non-training clause in the DPA for Gamma.

2) Retention: Default hosted retention for request/response payloads and debug logs is 30 days. KV cache is ephemeral per-session and not persisted beyond configured session boundaries. We provide options:
- Reduce hosted retention to 7 days
- Disable retention for request/response payloads (retains only minimal operational metadata)
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, you control retention and can configure 0-day retention of request content.
(Attached: retention-matrix.csv — shows defaults and configurable options.)

3) Deletion: Deletion requests are processed within 48 hours for active systems; we aim to purge from primary storage immediately and purge from hot backups within 30 days. Cold backups are handled per the SLA (we can specify accelerated deletion in contract). We provide an audit token and deletion certificate once complete.

4) Residency: Hosted API allows region pinning (us-east, us-west, eu-west). For Gamma’s requirement to remain in the US, we can pin to us-west (primary) with US-only backups. Telemetry processing for service telemetry is routed to US regions for US-pinned tenants. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.

5) Contract: We can add the requested clause to the DPA: sample language attached in the DPA draft. For customers who need additional contractual guarantees (e.g., explicit anti-training language + retention SLOs) we use a DPA addendum and can provide a DocuSign-ready DPA.

Next steps: I’ve attached a short SOC2 summary and the retention matrix. If you want a call, I can bring Lauren (solutions) and Markus (security) — propose Tue 14 Jul 10:00 PT.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0189

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf; retention-matrix.csv; DPA_draft_Gamma.docx

Vivek / Lauren — quick follow-up from Legal: the non-training statement is important but we need to ensure it covers both models and any derivative aggregated datasets used for internal analytics. Can you confirm wording that Redwood will not use Gamma content to train or fine-tune any models, nor include it in aggregated datasets used to train models?

Also: can you provide the audit trail for deletion (format and delivery)? We will want the cert as part of an acceptance criterion.

If you can confirm in writing, we can proceed with the DPA review.

Thanks,
Tom Chen
Senior Counsel, Gamma Analytics
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Chen <tom.chen@gamma-analytics.com>, Emily Reed <emily.reed@gamma-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data handling Q&A — non-training guarantee and retention windows

Tom / Emily — brief confirmations and next steps:

• Wording: We will accept contract language that reads: "Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content (including prompts, files, and generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any shared or base models, nor will Redwood include Customer Content in aggregated datasets used to train models." Our legal team will propose final DPA text; the DPA_draft_Gamma.docx attached in my prior email contains the proposed clause.

• Deletion audit: We will provide a deletion certificate that includes a timestamped audit token, the storage paths purged, and confirmation of purge from hot backups. Cold backups require the agreed SLA window (we can include an accelerated purge clause). Certificate delivery is via encrypted email or secure Drive link.

• Ops options: If Gamma requires zero retention in hosted mode we can configure request/response retention to 0 days; we recommend Dedicated/Private for the most stringent controls.

Next steps: I’ll route the DPA draft to our Legal (cc'd: Markus) for a short review cycle. I’ll also create the DocuSign envelope for the DPA addendum and share the Drive folder with the compliance binder. Proposed call remains Tue 14 Jul 10:00 PT — we can reschedule if that doesn’t work.

If that sounds good, I’ll mark this as the formal answer and move to DPA redlines.

Best,
Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
